prerequisites: Student has a structured knowledge of mathematics, including algebra and analysis.
Student has a structured knowledge of physics, mechanics.
Student has a structured knowledge of basis of machine design.

learning_outcomes.text: Student is able to define basic laws of fluid mechanics.
Student is able to explain the principles of machines operation and the phenomena utilized in their construction.
Student is able to Indicate the relationship between the fundamental laws of fluid mechanics and principles of operation of machines equipment.
Student is able to analyse the process of the phenomena associated with the flows in the machines operation.
Structured knowledge of machine design theory.
Student is able to combine law of fluid mechanics with the problems of machine design and operation.
Student understands the legal aspects and effects of engineering activities.
Student understands and is aware of the non-technical aspects and impacts of engineering activities in machine design.
Student is aware of the necessity of individual and group activities that go beyond the engineering operation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Properties of liquids and gases, forces and stresses in fluids, basic concepts of field theory.
Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids, fluid motion analysis method, streamlines, potential and rotational flow.
The basic equations of fluid mechanics, the continuity equation, the conservation of momentum equation for the ideal and real fluids (Euler equation and Navier-Stokes equations).
Hydrostatic equations, communicating vessels, the pressure forces of the liquid on the walls.
Buoyancy and stability of floating bodies.
Euler equation integrals - Bernoulli's equation, examples of applications: measurements of velocity, the flow of liquid through the holes.
The equations of momentum and moment of momentum equation, hydrodynamic reaction, principles of turbo-machinery, pumps and turbines.
Real fluids, laminar and turbulent flow, the Bernoulli's equation for real fluids.
The flow similitude, the dimensionless numbers in fluid Dynamics, examples of applications.
Examples of solutions of N-S equations , flows in the axially-symmetric pipes , major losses and their calculation, the effect of roughness.
Hydrodynamic theory of lubrication in bearings, flows through the narrow gaps.
Flow in pipes, pipelines characteristics, the unsteady phenomena - water hammer.
The theory of the boundary layer, laminar and turbulent layer, the phenomenon of flow separation.
Flow around bodies, drag forces, aerofoil theory, the hydrodynamic characteristics of profiles. Methods of calculation of forces on aerofoil.
Numerical methods in fluid mechanics, examples of use in the analysis of flows.
Final Test
The solution of the basic fluid properties problems.
Exercises illustrating the application of the Euler equation and Pascal's law.
Calculation of pressure forces on the walls.
Application of the Bernoulli's equation and the continuity equation for calculating ideal fluid flow.
Calculation of buoyancy and stability of floating bodies.
Application of the conservation of momentum equation and moment of momentum equation to calculate the hydrodynamic forces.
Calculation of the pressure loss in closed in pipelines. Determination of pipeline characteristics.
Final Test
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
assessment_rules: For the lecture, the final grade (P) is calculated as 0.5 * F1 + 0.5 * FC. For classes, the final grade (P) is equal to F1, which is also equal to FC. The way of evaluating educational effect achievement for both lecture and classes is through a test.
